known_bad.what: Every published stream in this project carries an Artifactory property named `layout.canonical_hash`, written by scripts/ci/gds_canonical_hash.py. The name reads like a layout identity and the value cannot support that reading. MEASURED 2026-08-26 on this candidate and its reference: KLayout strmxor 0.30.10 reports NO DIFFERENCES between _DRYRUN_20260826_rc1v3r4 and _DRYRUN_20260826_v3r4 across all 49 layer/datatype pairs, while the two canonical hashes are DIFFERENT (48891f86d4865fab0d607a56... vs 3f90ad3babba0298ca521098...) at identical byte count (302,688,050) and identical record count (34,791,830). The cause is known and is not in the tool: write_stream is not order-deterministic. Re-streaming one database on 26 Aug produced 26,842 differing bytes, 12,600 of them BGNLIB/BGNSTR clocks and 14,242 decoding as padring filler SREFs (PFILLER5_G, PFILLER20_G, PCORNER_G) emitted in another order in the top cell.
known_bad.decision: NOT withdrawn and NOT rewritten. The digest is CORRECT for what it computes and the raw md5/sha256 beside it are load-bearing -- a foundry Final Report cites the md5. What is wrong is the DIRECTION anyone may read into it, so the direction is now carried with the number instead of being left to the reader: gds_canonical_hash.py returns a `claim` field saying a MATCH implies the same layout and a MISMATCH implies nothing, and its --selftest gained an arm that proves the order sensitivity in a fixture (two files holding the same two rectangles in opposite record order: identical byte and record counts, different digest). The layout question is now answered properly and separately, by a geometric arbiter: scripts/ci/gds_xor_arbiter.py, wired in as the `gds-layout-identity` gate and proved both directions in its own selftest. An order-insensitive element-multiset digest IS the right cheap streaming answer if one is ever wanted -- it was run ad hoc on 26 Aug and returned IDENTICAL for 2,267 structures and 6,210,067 elements -- but it is a second approximation of a question the arbiter now answers exactly, so none was implemented. THE PUBLISH PATH WAS NOT TOUCHED: renaming a live store property is a store change, it would orphan the key on already-published artifacts, and a republish is being co-ordinated separately.
known_bad.withdraw_when: the store stops publishing this digest under a `layout.*` name -- either renamed to something that says RECORD SEQUENCE, or accompanied by the gds-layout-identity gate's verdict as a sibling property so a consumer reading the store sees the geometric answer next to the record one. Until then, treat a `layout.canonical_hash` mismatch as a prompt to run the arbiter and never as a finding.

Incomplete verification: 0` with `All primary outputs are mapped: yes`. The harness FAILs on three rules Conformal does not apply: (1) 96 extra unmapped GOLDEN DFFs, all of them u_nanosoc_eth_chiplet_chip/u_soc/u_tidechart/u_tidechart_controller/u_enum/root_port_cursor_r_reg[0..31][0..2] and no other point anywhere in the design; (2) unreachable key points not symmetric, 446 golden vs 319 revised; (3) tool exit code 40. Exit 40 decodes (Conformal_User/LEC_debug.html, installed at /eda/cadence/confrml/doc) as bit 3 `unmapped points or extra POs` plus bit 5 `abort or uncompared points exist during ANY comparison` -- bit 5 is STICKY and was set by intermediate hierarchical sub-compares (1378 and 1071 abort rows in logs/lec_syn.log) that `analyze abort -compare` then resolved; bit 6, `abort during the LAST comparison`, is CLEAR and both final tallies read 0 aborted / 0 uncompared. This is the same failure the 2026-08-21 lineage produced (build/gdsrun-20260821-slpads/reports/lec/syn/verdict.txt): identical 96 names, identical 5433/5433, identical 446/319, identical exit 40 -- on a DIFFERENT netlist (gate.v md5 91e0f49c here vs a7076071 there), so it is a property of the RTL and the parameterisation, not of one synthesis run.
known_bad.decision: ACCEPTED as parameterisation-bounded dead-code elimination. The 96 flops are dead IN THE RTL, and four independent measurements say so. (1) STRUCTURAL, from tidechart/src/rtl/tidechart_enum_fsm.sv (the file the dofile reads; unmodified since 2026-08-23 00:34, i.e. before this run's synthesis started at 00:51 on 26 Aug -- checked over all 430 RTL paths the dofile names, newest mtime 08-23): root_port_cursor_r[0:31] is [PORT_W-1:0] = 32 x 3 = exactly 96 bits, and its ENTIRE fanout is itself, root_own_port_subtree_r[assign_port] (line 1157) and root_port_subtree_r[p_id][assign_port] (line 1159), both behind the guard `assign_port < NUM_PORTS_V` at line 1154. (2) THE PARAMETER IS 1, not assumed: src/rtl/nanosoc_eth_chiplet.sv:1191 instantiates tidechart_shim with .NUM_PORTS(1), and the LEC output corroborates it independently -- root_own_port_subtree_r is [0:NUM_PORTS-1] x 32 bits and Conformal reports exactly 32 of them, which is only true at NUM_PORTS=1. At NUM_PORTS=1 the guard is `assign_port < 1`, i.e. assign_port==0; the p_id!=0 arm sets assign_port = cursor+1 when cursor==0 (UPLINK_PORT_ASSUMED is 0) and assign_port = cursor otherwise, so assign_port==0 is UNSATISFIABLE there and the write to the surviving array root_port_subtree_r never fires from the cursor path -- which is why root_port_subtree_r IS still in the netlist (it keeps its cursor-independent write at line 1177, feeding fc_tx_data) while the cursor is not. The cursor's only live consumer is therefore root_own_port_subtree_r. (3) THAT CONSUMER IS DEAD, measured by the tool: reports/lec/syn/lec_syn_unreachable_golden.rpt marks all 32 u_enum/root_own_port_subtree_r_reg, all 24 u_enum/subtree_wr_slice_o_reg and all 32 u_apb_regs/port_subtree_r_reg, 32 uplink_subtree_r_reg and 32 local_subtree_r_reg UNREACHABLE IN THE GOLDEN -- `all paths to outputs are blocked` -- 432 of the 446 golden-only unreachable points are inside u_tidechart. (4) THE REASON IS DOCUMENTED IN THE RTL AND IS AN ADDRESSING FACT, not a synthesis accident: tidechart_apb_regs.sv decodes the subtree region at word addresses 7'h40..7'h49 (byte 0x100-0x124) off a 9-bit apb_paddr_ext, and tidechart_controller.sv passes APB_ADDR_W=8, so the pad at line 398 forces bit 8 to 0 and, in that file's own words, `the new decode branches simply never match and the region is unreachable via APB`. Its snapshot outputs are unconnected at this integration (the ahb-chiplet-irqc block is absent; nanosoc_eth_chiplet.sv ties tc_to_irqc_tready_i to 0). So TC_PORT_SUBTREE_*, TC_PORT_SUBTREE_UP and TC_LOCAL_SUBTREE are not readable on this die BY CONSTRUCTION, the enumeration subtree cone that feeds them is unobservable, and the cursor that indexes it is dead. Synthesis is right to delete it: the netlist carries 0 root_port_cursor, 0 root_own_port_subtree and 0 u_apb_regs port/uplink/local_subtree flops, and every primary output plus every mapped state point compares equivalent. THE CHAIN IS COMPLETE AND IT COMPOSES, which it did not for any previous lineage: gate (_gate.v -> _gate_power.v) PASS 61,599/61,599 exit 0, and pnr (_gate_power.v -> _pnr.v) PASS 61,599/61,599 exit 0, both on this run's own files and both joined by sha1 -- _gate.v 58724c88 is the syn leg's revised and the gate leg's golden, _gate_power.v f5875467 is the gate leg's revised and the pnr leg's golden, _pnr.v 2053949d is the netlist behind the shipped stream (the rc1eco-20260826 tree writes GDS only; it contains no write_netlist and no instance-level ECO command). Evidence in build/gdsrun-20260826-rc1/reports/lec/{syn,gate,pnr}/. NOT ACCEPTED, and deliberately not claimed: this says nothing about whether the TideChart subtree registers SHOULD be dead. They are a functional hole -- an RTL register file the CPU cannot read because the bus is one bit too narrow -- and that is a separate open item, not a LEC finding.
known_bad.withdraw_when: any of: (a) NUM_PORTS at src/rtl/nanosoc_eth_chiplet.sv's tidechart_shim instance stops being 1 -- at NUM_PORTS>1 the guard `assign_port < NUM_PORTS_V` becomes satisfiable for a non-root parent, root_port_subtree_r (which IS in the netlist and DOES reach fc_tx_data) starts depending on the cursor, and deleting it would change silicon behaviour; (b) APB_ADDR_W at tidechart_controller.sv rises to 9 or more, which makes the 0x100 subtree region decodable and the whole cone observable; (c) the subtree snapshot outputs (port_subtree_o / local_subtree_o / uplink_subtree_o) get a consumer, e.g. the ahb-chiplet-irqc block being integrated; (d) the unmapped set stops being exactly the 96 root_port_cursor_r_reg names -- ANY other unmapped point, or any non-equivalent or aborted compare point, is a new finding and this acceptance does not cover it; (e) the design is re-synthesised, in which case re-run all three legs: the acceptance is bound to gate.v sha1 58724c88514ca0976f292009654f9e5fec463138.

xor_reference.why: CHOSEN, not defaulted, and the choice is the claim. The two available references answer different questions. (a) A RE-STREAM of this run's own ECO'd database would prove only that write_stream renders that database faithfully -- a self-consistency check that can catch a writer bug and nothing else, and it needs an Innovus session on a read-only tree. (b) _DRYRUN_20260826_v3r4 (md5 70858177e4b9cca11daf201f52eeb45d) is the SAME INTENDED LAYOUT REACHED BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE: it descends from gdsrun-20260825-resynth via a hand ECO on the pgeco database, while this candidate is a full flow from RTL a day later with the same edits landed in-flow through hooks/post_powerplan.tcl plus one marker-driven post-route ECO. A zero XOR between them is therefore a REPRODUCIBILITY result, and it is the stronger of the two: it says two independent syntheses, placements, CTSs and routes converge on the same polygons, and it carries every geometric measurement made on _v3r4 -- its Calibre four-tier 737/46/13/0 and its LVS -- across to these bytes unchanged. WHAT A ZERO DOES NOT PROVE, either way: that either stream is CORRECT (DRC, LVS and LEC answer that, and lec-rtl-to-gate is still NOT-MEASURED here), and nothing about the foundry's merged view, which adds dummy fill and a seal ring that are not in these bytes.
